title: Windows companion credential and lease inheritance
failure_observed: The original Windows run and companion directories retained explicit allow entries for principals other than the controller. Generated credentials inherited those entries and the CLI rejected them before it contacted the hub.
correction: The host and hub create fresh run, engine-credential, and companion directories, then replace and verify their protected DACL before writing credentials. The sole allow entry uses the current process token user SID with FullControl, container and object inheritance, and no propagation restrictions.

checks: The unchanged credential reader accepted the generated run manifest, engine credential and companion credential.
The normal CLI observed a synthetic native state through the temporary loopback host, attached a controller, reloaded and renewed the lease, and released it.
The same reader rejected a separate empty JSON file after the test added a Builtin Users read ACE.
verification.scope: A fresh temporary host on real Windows ran the integration test. No live match or recorded arena was required for these permission checks.
